fieldData.awb---key-feature-1-content:
Every software request gets an IT check first

Priya Nair in marketing writes that her team needs 12 more seats on its design tool, about $2,160 a year. The app tags the request as software, finds the supplier on the approved list, and sends it to Tom Becker in IT security before the budget owner sees it. Nothing sits in a shared procurement inbox.
fieldData.awb---integration-feature-1:
Three supplier quotes land in one table

Facilities requires three quotes on anything over $10,000. For a yearly HVAC service contract, one scope goes to Northwind Mechanical, Globex Climate, and Initech Air. The replies come back at $14,200, $12,850, and $13,400, and Marcus Lee awards the work to Globex Climate.
fieldData.awb---integration-feature-2:
Under $500 from the catalog, the PO goes straight out

Lab staff order from a catalog of contracted items at the prices Cedar Lab Supply agreed to. Jonah Reyes picks four boxes of pipette tips at $38.50 a box, $154 in all. Catalog orders under $500 need no approval, and PO-3107 goes to Cedar Lab Supply as soon as he submits.
fieldData.acrm---integration-feature-4:
A card purchase off contract reaches the category owner

Each Monday the app checks last week's company card spend against the contracted vendor list. A $640 office chair from a retail site is flagged, since Brightwell Office holds the furniture contract at $455 for the same model. Rosa Mendez, who owns furniture, gets a direct message with the $185 gap.
